ELECTION RESEARCH: 2026 B.C. provincial general election

Background for the roundup's election stories and any race the hosts mention. It is not the deep dive's subject.

**Cariboo-Chilcotin**

Candidates on the filed list, per the roll-call sources: Kathryn Askew (BC NDP), Lorne Doerkson (Conservative), Douglas Gook (BC Green). The Elections BC candidate report lists all three for this riding (elections.bc.ca candidate report, Oct. 2026). Studio X News carries the same three (studioxnews.ca, final candidate list).

- **Kathryn Askew (BC NDP).** 100 Mile Free Press (Oct. 1, 2026) reports she is a retired school teacher from Canim Lake, named the NDP candidate in a party news release. It says she has 32 years in education, served in leadership roles with the BC Teachers' Federation and her local union, and volunteers with local fire, legion and community clubs. The same article says she has received a national teaching award. No previous election run by Askew has been established in the sources checked.
- **Lorne Doerkson (Conservative).** Sourced background: MLA for Cariboo-Chilcotin since 2020, first elected as a B.C. Liberal, re-elected in 2024 as a B.C. Conservative (Elections BC results, 2024-10-19). Vancouver Sun reports he was first elected in 2020 with 51.25 per cent of the vote, running for the B.C. Liberals (Vancouver Sun, undated in snippet). Elections BC's 2020 statement of votes shows him at 6,600 votes (51.25%) (elections.bc.ca statement of votes, 2020). The Ashcroft-Cache Creek Journal (Oct. 20, 2024) reports he crossed the floor on May 31, 2024 to join the B.C. Conservatives and was re-elected in 2024. BC Ballot gives the 2024 Conservative margin in the riding as 7,722 votes (bcballot.ca). The Globe and Mail (Sept. 26, 2026) reports he took over as Conservative leader and is leading the party into this election. No controversy involving Doerkson was established in the sources checked.
- **Douglas Gook (BC Green).** My Cariboo Now (Oct. 6, 2020) reports this was his fourth run for the BC Greens in the North Cariboo riding. The Elections BC 2020 statement of votes shows him at 707 votes, 6.38%, in Cariboo North (elections.bc.ca statement of votes, 2020). Caledonia Courier (Oct. 2024) reports he had run unsuccessfully four times in North Cariboo, including a 2017 Nechako Lakes bid where he took about nine per cent. CKPG Today (Sept. 13, 2024) announced him as the Green candidate for Nechako Lakes in 2024. He is also described as a Quesnel resident. No controversy was established in the sources checked.

**Prince George-North Cariboo (includes Quesnel)**

Candidates on the filed list: Sheldon Clare (Conservative), Denice Bardua (BC NDP), Randy Thompson (BC Green). The Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports the list was confirmed by Elections BC after nominations closed on Oct. 3. CKPG Today (Oct. 3, 2026) lists the same three.

- **Sheldon Clare (Conservative, incumbent).** Sourced background: won the riding for the B.C. Conservatives in 2024 (Elections BC results, 2024-10-19). Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports he won 11,430 votes, or 56.82%, in 2024, ahead of independent Coralee Oakes at 21.84%. Times Colonist (Jan. 8, 2026, Canadian Press) reports he said he was running for the B.C. Conservative leadership, and CFJC Today (Feb. 28, 2026) reports he and fellow MLA Steve Kooner withdrew from that race. Prince George Citizen (June 29, 2026) reports he was named the party's house leader. No controversy involving Clare was established in the sources checked.
- **Denice Bardua (BC NDP).** CKPG Today (Sept. 24, 2024) reports she was announced as the NDP candidate for this riding in 2024. Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports she finished third in 2024 with 17.03%. BC Ballot lists her in the riding (bcballot.ca). Business in Vancouver's 2024 riding brief describes her as an employee of the Quesnel school board. No controversy was established in the sources checked.
- **Randy Thompson (BC Green).** Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports he finished fourth in 2024 with just over four per cent of the vote. BC Greens' candidate page (bcgreens.ca) says he ran as the Green candidate in this riding in 2024 and previously served two years on the party's provincial council. PG Daily News (Oct. 11, 2026) reports the Greens announced him as the candidate. No controversy was established in the sources checked.

**Roster and articles**

The My Cariboo Now article on First Nations leaders and a candidate over alleged residential school denialism (Oct. 13, 2026) does not name a candidate for either of these two ridings in the excerpt I could read. The version I read names a candidate in a different riding, so I have not attached it to either race. The My Cariboo Now B.C. NDP climate pledge article (Oct. 13, 2026) names no candidates in the excerpt.

The show has not yet established any previous election run for Kathryn Askew.
